newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.5 pct on minor cash entry.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.5 pct on minor cash entry.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted gains in a continued technical rebound on Wednesday with the help of limited cash entry, but the upside was capped by firm resistance at the index's 65,000 level, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed 974.22 points, or 1.53 percent higher at 64,616.63, down slightly from a morning high of 64,680. Trade volume leapt further to 8.91 trillion lira from Tuesday's 6.12 trillion.
Brokers said selling sparked by news that Iraqi forces fired one or two anti-aircraft missiles at U.S. fighter jets over northern Iraq was quickly overcome by selective purchases.
"If cash influx continues, the 65,000-65,500 barrier may be tested this week. Privatisation news also helped to move the market," said Huseyin Istanbullu from Meksa securities.

State Minister Ufuk Soylemez said the privatisation agency OIB would draw up and announce next week a sell-off calendar for 1996 and coming years. His statements kept activity focused on shares of largely state owned companies.

The Higher Board of privatisation met for the first time on Wednesday since Turkey's Islamist-led government was formed in June. The government is seeking ways of speeding up sell-offs to close big state deficits.

A technical rebound began after support of the index was confirmed at 62,500 on Monday. The index regained 1.17 percent on Tuesday following Monday's 0.84 percent drop on top of last week's 1.7 percent loss.

The 85-share industrial index rose 1.52 percent to 71,224.92 and the 15-share financial index gained 1.55 percent to 56,534.10. Of the 217 shares traded, 89 advanced, 63 declined and 65 were unchanged.

Top actives were utility Aktas Elektrik, up 10,000 lira at 450,000, partially privatised flat steel giant Eregli, up 600 lira at 9,100, largely state-owned petroleum refiner Tupras, up 250 lira at 14,750 and Turkish Airlines which firmed 250 lira to 25,000. -- Aydan Eksin, Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 0875.
